newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off but fight Dow slump.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off but fight Dow slump.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed lower on profit-taking for the second session in a row Wednesday, but managed to pare earlier losses and showed resilience in the face of a slump on Wall Street.
"The market is holding up, it is ratifiying its primary upward channel and a consolidation zone between 3,700-3,750 points," a technical analyst said.
"All that's happening now is price stabilisation, where stragglers are leading the market," he added.
The leading IPC share index ended down 9.36 points, or 0.25 percent, at 3,707.98.
Some dealers said a reduced but unbroken flow of foreign investment had bolstered share prices.
"The market feels firm even though it's been hit by profit-taking. Foreign investors are still stepping in to buy stragglers or stocks with a bright outlook," said a trader from the Vector brokerage.
"We still mustn't lose sight of international factors. Even though we are somewhat decoupled from the Dow, its slump hit us this morning," another trader said.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 33.87 points at 6,850.03 points, on disappointing fourth quarter results posted by International Business Machines Corp..
In Mexico, a total of 108 stocks changed hands on the broad market, of which 45 ended up and an equal number declined.

Financial group Serfin headed the decliners, sliding 18 centavos to 2.87 pesos (37 cents), followed by hotel group Posadas, off 16 centavos to 3.72 pesos (48 cents), which traders said had a poor outlook for fourth quarter earnings.
Simec, steelmaking arm of the debt-troubled Sidek group, headed the gainers, up 17 centavos (2 cents) to 1.68 pesos (22 cents).
Simec was followed by conglomerate Accelsa and chemical firm Cydsa, which gained 11 centavos (1 cent) and 1.98 pesos (24 cents), respectively, to 1.86 (24 cents) and 21.00 pesos ($2.69).
"Accelsa was just catching up with the market, but there is something to Cydsa. It has been heavily traded, and more extensive debt restructuring has been discounted for some time," a broker said.
